facts.t: A day on Venus (one full spin) lasts about 243 Earth days – longer than its year of about 225 days.
Sunlight needs about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth – about 3.8 cm every year.
Jupiter is so big that more than 1,300 Earths could fit inside it.
Saturn is, on average, less dense than water.
Comets are balls of ice, dust and rock. Their tails always point away from the Sun.
Footprints left on the Moon by the Apollo astronauts could last for millions of years – there is no wind to blow them away.
Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest volcano in the solar system – about 22 km high, roughly two and a half times Mount Everest.
The International Space Station circles Earth about every 90 minutes, so the crew can see around 16 sunrises a day.
Neutron stars are so dense that a teaspoon of their matter would weigh about a billion tonnes on Earth.
Our galaxy, the Milky Way, holds an estimated 100 to 400 billion stars.
Sound cannot travel through the near-vacuum of space, so a real space battle would be completely silent.
Most shooting stars are tiny grains of dust, often smaller than a grain of sand, burning up high in the atmosphere.
Mars looks red because its dust contains iron oxide – in other words, rust.
The Sun holds about 99.8% of all the mass in our solar system.
Halley's Comet comes back roughly every 76 years. Its next visit is expected around 2061.
A lightning bolt can heat the air to around 30,000 °C – about five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
Lightning flashes somewhere on Earth about 45 times every second.
Fresh lava from Hawaiian volcanoes is about 1,100–1,200 °C hot.
About 80% of the volcanic eruptions on Earth happen deep under the sea.
An ordinary fluffy cloud can hold around 500 tonnes of water.
Some kinds of bamboo can grow almost a metre in a single day.
Snow crystals almost always have six sides because of the way water molecules link together in ice.
Electric eels can give a shock of up to about 860 volts.
The northern lights appear when charged particles from the Sun hit gases high up in our atmosphere.
Honey keeps for a very long time because it holds little water and is slightly acidic, so germs struggle to grow in it.
Cinnamon is the dried inner bark of trees from the Cinnamomum family.
Ginger is not really a root: it is a rhizome, an underground stem.
Wool can soak up around 30% of its own weight in moisture without feeling wet.
Chimpanzees, dolphins, elephants, crows and octopuses are counted among the most intelligent animals.
An octopus has three hearts and blue blood.
Crows can recognise individual human faces and remember them for years.
Elephants can recognise themselves in a mirror – something only a handful of species have shown.
Bottlenose dolphins use their own 'signature whistles', which work a bit like names.
facts.s: Univ. of St Andrews – dolphin signature whistles

facts.t: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived – up to about 30 metres long.
Hummingbirds can hover in place and even fly backwards.
Sloths move so slowly that tiny algae grow in their fur, giving them a greenish tint.
Tiny tardigrades, also called water bears, survived a trip outside a spacecraft in open space.
Honeybees tell each other where flowers are with a 'waggle dance'.
Owls cannot move their eyes, so they turn their heads instead – up to about 270 degrees.
facts.s: Johns Hopkins Medicine – owl neck study

facts.t: Emperor penguins can dive deeper than 500 metres.
In a 2021 study, pigs learned to steer a cursor on a screen with a joystick.
Arctic terns fly about 70,000 km a year between the Arctic and Antarctica – the longest migration known.
Cats often sleep 12 to 16 hours a day – so Magic napping in grandma's basket is perfectly normal.
facts.s: Veterinary references (e.g. Cornell Feline Health Center)

facts.t: A cat's purr usually has a low frequency of about 25 to 150 hertz.
Cats have a third eyelid, a thin membrane that helps protect and moisten the eye.
Cats cannot taste sweetness – the gene for the sweet taste receptor does not work in cats. Magic is only after the crumbs for fun.
A cat's whiskers sense tiny movements in the air and help it judge whether it fits through a gap.
Adult cats rarely meow at each other – meowing is mostly how they talk to people.
Cats began living alongside people roughly 10,000 years ago in the Near East, around the time of the first farms.
A cat can jump several times its own height in a single leap.
Each cat ear is moved by about 30 muscles, so it can swivel to catch the faintest sound.
Cats hear sounds up to about 64,000 hertz – far higher than humans, who stop at around 20,000.
Kittens are born with blue eyes. Their real eye colour – like Magic's green – appears over the following weeks.
Snakes smell with their tongues: the forked tongue carries scent to a special organ in the roof of the mouth.
Snakes have no eyelids. A clear scale covers and protects each eye, which is why they never blink.
Pythons, boas and pit vipers can sense the body heat of their prey with special pit organs.
Snakes can swallow prey wider than their own head: the two halves of the lower jaw are joined by stretchy ligaments.
Snakes shed their skin several times a year, often in one single piece.
The reticulated python is among the longest snakes in the world – it can grow longer than 6 metres.
Snakes have no outer ears, but they can feel vibrations from the ground through their jawbones.
There are about 4,000 kinds of snakes, and most of them are not dangerous to people.
Earthworms have no lungs – they breathe through their moist skin.
An earthworm has five pairs of heart-like pumps that push blood through its body.
Charles Darwin studied earthworms for decades and wrote a whole book about them in 1881.
facts.s: C. Darwin, The Formation of Vegetable Mould through the Action of Worms (1881)

facts.t: Ants can carry objects many times heavier than their own body.
Scientists estimate that around 10 quintillion insects (a 1 followed by 19 zeros) are alive at any moment.
Dragonflies are among the best hunters in nature – they catch their prey up to about 95% of the time.
Fireflies make light with a chemical reaction that gives off almost no heat.
A cockroach can survive for days, even about a week, without its head.
Butterflies taste with their feet: sensors on their legs tell them if a leaf is good for their eggs.
Bees can see ultraviolet light, which reveals patterns on flowers that are invisible to us.
The term UFO – unidentified flying object – was coined by the US Air Force in the 1950s.
facts.s: US Air Force, 1950s (Project Blue Book era)

facts.t: Scientists listen for signals from other civilisations with radio telescopes. So far no signal has been confirmed – but the UFO in our games keeps trying.
Gingerbread has been baked in Europe since the Middle Ages, and the German city of Nuremberg became famous for it.
One sheep usually gives about 2 to 7 kg of wool a year – enough for several of grandma's sweaters.
facts.s: The Woolmark Company / sheep breeding references

facts.t: The spark from a doorknob can be several thousand volts, but the current is so tiny that it is harmless.
In a copper wire the electrons themselves only creep along at a fraction of a millimetre per second – yet the lamp lights up almost instantly.
Number grids where each digit appears once per row and column are called Latin squares. Leonhard Euler studied them in the 18th century.
facts.s: Euler, Recherches sur une nouvelle espèce de quarrés magiques (1782)

facts.t: Dogs can be trained to find people buried under snow or rubble – their sense of smell is many thousands of times better than ours.
Rats remember the way through a maze using special 'place cells' in the brain – a discovery awarded the Nobel Prize in 2014.
facts.s: Cognitive science – mazes and spatial memory
